old: Greenfield execution on borrowed time. The Virginia plant (reported at ~$500M, up to 700 tons of propellant a year, start of production 2028) costs €450–550M, about a third of today's €1.46bn market cap, and is being built before any customer has signed a binding production contract. New solid-motor capacity in the US has a history of delays: qualification of each motor takes years, and a plant that starts late carries its fixed costs (€7–9M of Avio USA opex already in 2026) with no revenue behind them. A 12-month slip plus a 20% overrun moves the value toward the €13.3 bear case and probably means a third capital raise in two years.

old: Industry and legal-regime risk. Litigation funding is under political pressure in the US (state bills such as Colorado HB 1421 in 2026; recurring federal proposals to tax or disclose funding) and in the UK after PACCAR. Burford's largest recent upside events (Taction, Cameroon, the UK Google claim, German assignment-model cases) each depend on courts or sovereigns paying. A rule change that caps funder returns or forces disclosure would lower the ~82% ROIC the thesis leans on; a sovereign that refuses to pay (Argentina, Cameroon) turns a paper award into years of enforcement costs.

old: Control without accountability. old: Avio is Europe's solid-rocket-motor house with a launcher attached.
